sections.title: باب 11 — متن (13)

paras.text: (continued from p.235) … tax, and central excise tax on tea, tobacco and betel nut.
paras.urdu: (ص 235 سے جاری) … ٹیکس، چائے، تمباکو اور چھالیا پر مرکزی ایکسائز ٹیکس۔

During 2009-10 a total of 697.9 billion (arab) rupees were transferred to the provincial governments.

paras.pashto: د ملي مالي کمیسیون (NFC) د پرېکړې له مخې د مرکزي حکومت او ولایتي حکومتونو ترمنځ ”فدرالي د وېش وړ پیسې“ (Federal Divisible Pool) په لاندې نسبت وېشل کېږي: پنجاب ولایت ۵۱.۷۴ سلنه، سند ۲۴.۵۵ سلنه، خیبر پښتونخوا ۱۴.۶۲ سلنه او بلوچستان ۹.۰۹ سلنه. د ۲۰۰۹-۱۰ په جریان کې ولایتي حکومتونو ته ټول ۶۹۷.۹ بلیونه (میلیارده) روپۍ ولېږدول شوې.

paras.text: 2. Water rate (Water Rate)
paras.urdu: 2۔ آبیانہ (Water Rate):
paras.pashto: ۲. د اوبو محصول (Water Rate)

paras.text: The provincial governments have constructed many canals in their areas, from which cultivators get water to irrigate their lands, and pay its compensation to the government in the form of water rate.

paras.text: 3. Land revenue (Land Revenue)
paras.urdu: 3۔ مالیہ زمین (Land Revenue):
paras.pashto: ۳. د ځمکې مالیه (Land Revenue)

paras.urdu: 4۔ موٹر گاڑیوں پر محصولات (Taxes on Motor Vehicles):

paras.pashto: په دې کې د موټرو د راجسټرېشن فیس، د سړک مالیه، د ډرېوري جواز د ترلاسه کولو فیس او جریمې او نور شامل وي.

paras.text: 5. Stamps and court fee (Stamp Paper and Court Fee)
paras.urdu: 5۔ اشٹام اور کورٹ فیس (Stamp Paper and Court Fee):
paras.pashto: ۵. ټاپه او د محکمې فیس (Stamp Paper and Court Fee)

paras.text: 6. Registration
paras.urdu: 6۔ رجسٹریشن:
paras.pashto: ۶. راجسټرېشن

paras.text: 7. Departments of economic services (Economic Services)

paras.pashto: ۷. د اقتصادي خدمتونو (Economic Services) څانګې

paras.text: 8. Departments of social services (Social Services)

paras.pashto: ۸. د ټولنیزو خدمتونو (Social Services) څانګې

paras.text: 9. Departments of civil administration (Civil Administration)

paras.pashto: ۹. د ملکي ادارې (Civil Administration) څانګې

(continued from p.235) … tax, and central excise tax on tea, tobacco and betel nut.

According to the decision of the National Finance Commission (NFC), the “federal divisible amount” (Federal Divisible Pool) is divided between the central government and the provincial governments in the following ratio: province of Punjab 51.74 per cent, Sindh 24.55 per cent, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 14.62 per cent and Balochistan 9.09 per cent. During 2009-10 a total of 697.9 billion (arab) rupees were transferred to the provincial governments.

2. Water rate (Water Rate)

The provincial governments have constructed many canals in their areas, from which cultivators get water to irrigate their lands, and pay its compensation to the government in the form of water rate.

3. Land revenue (Land Revenue)

In it, besides the rent or compensation of land, the sale of government lands and fines are included. The compensation for grazing cattle on government lands too is counted in this same head.

4. Revenues on motor vehicles (Taxes on Motor Vehicles)

In it the registration fee of vehicles, road tax, the fee for obtaining a driving licence, fines etc. are included.

5. Stamps and court fee (Stamp Paper and Court Fee)

The judicial and non-judicial applications which ordinary people give to the government, government tickets have to be affixed on them. Thus from their sale provincial governments obtain income. The sale of stamps too is a reasonable means of the government’s income.

6. Registration

In it the following are included: the fee for getting documents registered, the fee for providing a copy of registered documents, the fee for searching old records.

7. Departments of economic services (Economic Services)

These are included in them: agriculture, fishing, animal husbandry, communications and forests. From forests building wood, fuel, resin, turpentine and charcoal are obtained, and from their sale the government gets income. Road transport too is a reasonable means of income, and income is obtained from the contracts of fishing places of rivers.

8. Departments of social services (Social Services)

In them the departments of public health and public education are included. Although these too are spending departments, yet from here too some income is obtained in the form of fees.

9. Departments of civil administration (Civil Administration)

These departments are included in them: public administration, police, jails and courts. Otherwise these departments are spending ones, but from them a little income is received in the form of fees and fines.

10. Interest on loans (Debt Services)

The government gives loans to municipalities and semi-government corporations. Further, under the law of agricultural reform loans it gives loans to cultivators, on which it gets compensation.

11. Miscellaneous sources of income

In them entertainment tax, tax on the use of electricity, tax on petrol, tax on agricultural income, arms licence fee and tax on high-class hotels are included.

12. Grants of the federal government

By them are meant those amounts which the central government gives to provincial governments in emergency conditions, e.g. war, famine, flood and earthquake, for the rehabilitation and settlement of people.

Heads of expenditures of provincial governments (Heads of Expenditures of Provincial Governments)

The important heads of expenditure of provincial governments are explained below:

1. Tax-collecting departments

In this head that amount is included which is spent on the staff and other needs of the tax-collecting departments. Approximately two per cent of the total amount is spent on these departments.

2. Services of loans

The provincial governments pay interest on the loans which they take from the central government and other sources. Ten per cent of total expenditure is consumed on this.

3. Public administration (Civil Administration)

The departments which have been established for provincial administration, a considerable expenditure is incurred on them; approximately sixteen per cent of total expenditure is specified for this head.

4. Departments of social services (Social Services)

These are included in them: department of education, department of health, departments of scientific development, pension of retired employees. On this head approximately thirty-six per cent of total expenditure is spent.

5. Departments of economic services (Economic Services)

By them are meant these departments: irrigation, civil works, agriculture, communications and news-giving. On the provision of these services approximately thirty-four per cent of total expenditure is consumed.

Like the central government, provincial governments too make development budgets, in which amounts are provided for the development of these sectors: communications and news-giving, physical planning, agriculture, water, education and training, health, industries and minerals, the People’s Works Programme, social welfare and manpower etc.

10. Interest on loans (Debt Services)

The government gives loans to municipalities and semi-government corporations. Further, under the law of agricultural reform loans it gives loans to cultivators, on which it gets compensation.

11. Miscellaneous sources of income

In them entertainment tax, tax on the use of electricity, tax on petrol, tax on agricultural income, arms licence fee and tax on high-class hotels are included.

12. Grants of the federal government

By them are meant those amounts which the central government gives to provincial governments in emergency conditions, e.g. war, famine, flood and earthquake, for the rehabilitation and settlement of people.

Heads of expenditures of provincial governments (Heads of Expenditures of Provincial Governments)

The important heads of expenditure of provincial governments are explained below:

1. Tax-collecting departments

In this head that amount is included which is spent on the staff and other needs of the tax-collecting departments. Approximately two per cent of the total amount is spent on these departments.

2. Services of loans

The provincial governments pay interest on the loans which they take from the central government and other sources. Ten per cent of total expenditure is consumed on this.

3. Public administration (Civil Administration)

The departments which have been established for provincial administration, a considerable expenditure is incurred on them; approximately sixteen per cent of total expenditure is specified for this head.

4. Departments of social services (Social Services)

These are included in them: department of education, department of health, departments of scientific development, pension of retired employees. On this head approximately thirty-six per cent of total expenditure is spent.

5. Departments of economic services (Economic Services)

By them are meant these departments: irrigation, civil works, agriculture, communications and news-giving. On the provision of these services approximately thirty-four per cent of total expenditure is consumed.

Like the central government, provincial governments too make development budgets, in which amounts are provided for the development of these sectors: communications and news-giving, physical planning, agriculture, water, education and training, health, industries and minerals, the People’s Works Programme, social welfare and manpower etc.

10۔ قرضہ پر سود (Debt Services):

حکومت میونسپلٹیوں اور نیم سرکاری کارپوریشنوں کو قرضہ دیتی ہے۔ نیز زرعی اصلاحی قرضہ کے قانون کے تحت کاشت کاروں کو قرضہ دیتی ہے جس پر اسے معاوضہ ملتا ہے۔

11۔ آمدنی کے متفرق ذرائع:

ان میں تفریحی ٹیکس، بجلی کے استعمال پر ٹیکس، پٹرول پر ٹیکس، زرعی آمدنی پر ٹیکس، اسلحہ لائسنس فیس اور اعلیٰ قسم کے ہوٹلوں پر ٹیکس شامل ہیں۔

12۔ وفاقی حکومت کے عطیات:

ان سے مراد وہ رقوم ہیں جو مرکزی حکومت صوبائی حکومتوں کو ہنگامی حالات، مثلاً جنگ، قحط، سیلاب اور زلزلے کے زمانے میں لوگوں کی بحالی اور آبادی کے لئے دیتی ہے۔

صوبائی حکومتوں کے اخراجات کی مدیں (Heads of Expenditures of Provincial Governments)

صوبائی حکومتوں کے اخراجات کی اہم مدوں کی وضاحت ذیل میں کی گئی ہے:

1۔ ٹیکس اکٹھا کرنے والے محکمے:

اس مد میں وہ رقم شامل کی جاتی ہے جو ٹیکس اکٹھا کرنے والے محکموں کے عملے اور دیگر ضروریات پر خرچ کی جاتی ہے۔ کل رقم کا تقریباً دو فیصد حصہ ان محکموں پر صرف ہو جاتا ہے۔

2۔ قرضہ کی خدمات:

صوبائی حکومتیں مرکزی حکومت سے اور دیگر ذرائع سے جو قرضہ لیتی ہیں ان پر سود ادا کرتی ہیں۔ اس پر کل خرچ کا دس فیصد صرف ہوتا ہے۔

3۔ نظم و نسقِ عامہ (Civil Administration):

صوبائی نظم و نسق کے لیے جو محکمے قائم کئے گئے ہیں، ان پر کافی خرچ اٹھتا ہے، کل خرچ کا تقریباً سولہ فیصد اس مد کے لئے مخصوص ہوتا ہے۔

4۔ معاشرتی خدمات (Social Services) کے محکمے:

ان میں یہ شامل ہیں: محکمہ تعلیم، محکمہ صحت، سائنسی ترقی کے محکمے، ریٹائرڈ ملازموں کی پنشن۔ اس مد پر کل خرچ کا تقریباً چھتیس فیصد حصہ خرچ ہو جاتا ہے۔

5۔ معاشی خدمات (Economic Services) کے محکمے:

ان سے مراد یہ محکمے ہیں: آب پاشی، سول ورکس، زراعت، مواصلات اور خبر رسانی۔ ان خدمات کی بہم رسانی پر کل خرچ کا تقریباً چونتیس فیصد حصہ صرف ہوتا ہے۔
